advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Show the 'Gerrit token already replaced; SSM NOT updated' notice on every failure between the delete-token/generate step and a successful SSM put, not just on the shape check
evidence: infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:58: generated="$($GERRIT_SSH gerrit set-account "$BOT_USER" --generate-http-password)"  — a non-zero exit here ends the script through set -e without the notice
infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:77-82: printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | aws ssm put-parameter ... — a failure here also ends the script through set -e, after Gerrit's token was replaced, with no notice
infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:66-68: the 'already replaced ... SSM was NOT updated' message exists only inside the shape-check branch
advisory.finding: The new 'already replaced / SSM was NOT updated' notice only fires when the generator output has the wrong shape. Two other failures leave the bot in the same broken state with no notice: (1) `--generate-http-password` exits non-zero after `--delete-token default` already succeeded, and (2) `aws ssm put-parameter` fails after Gerrit issued the new token. Both abort silently through `set -e`, so the operator still doesn't learn that the bot can no longer authenticate.
scenarios: A transient SSH error or Gerrit error on --generate-http-password after delete-token succeeded
Expired or missing AWS credentials on the operator workstation make put-parameter fail after the token was rotated in Gerrit
advisory.suggested_fix: Before step 3, set `rotated_unsynced=1` and add `trap '[ "${rotated_unsynced:-0}" = 1 ] && echo "service-user: Gerrit token for $BOT_USER may already be replaced and SSM was NOT updated; re-run until this succeeds." >&2' EXIT`. Clear the flag right after a successful `aws ssm put-parameter`, and chain the cleanup into the later `trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT` so it doesn't replace this one.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `f"{GENERATED}\r"` (prefix-less, CR-terminated) to the fail-closed parametrize list so a test pins the CR-strip-before-prefix-check ordering
evidence: Removed line in diff: -TOKEN="${TOKEN%$'\r'}" (the old code already stripped CR from a prefixed token, so test_service_user_strips_a_trailing_carriage_return passes on both old and new code)
tests/scripts/test_operator_credential_argv.py:155: generated=f"New password: {GENERATED}\r" (prefixed; does not exercise prefix-less + CR)
tests/scripts/test_operator_credential_argv.py:139: GENERATED,  # token-shaped, but the "New password: " prefix is missing (no CR variant in the list)
advisory.finding: No test pins the new ordering, where the CR is stripped from `generated` before `TOKEN == generated` is checked. Consider a prefix-less, token-shaped line ending in CR (`f"{GENERATED}\r"`). The current script rejects it. But if the strip went back to acting on TOKEN only (`TOKEN="${TOKEN%$'\r'}"` after the prefix strip, as before), TOKEN would become GENERATED while `generated` would still be `GENERATED\r`. The equality check would then miss the missing prefix, and that line would be stored in SSM. Every current test still passes under that mutation. The new CR test uses a correctly prefixed line, which both the old and new code accept.
scenarios: A refactor moves the CR strip back after the prefix strip. A Gerrit/ssh path that prints a bare token followed by CRLF would then put the unprefixed value into SSM, and every test would stay green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `f"{GENERATED}\r",  # prefix missing; CR must not hide that` to the `generated` parametrize list in test_service_user_fails_closed_on_unexpected_generator_output.
